facts: The guide walks through the core workflow, from running a first package to managing several versions. [L6]
On a fresh install the local index is empty, so commands need the remote flag to query the registry directly. [L9]
Once a package is installed, commands that operate on it work without the remote flag. [L9]
package exec downloads a missing package automatically and runs the command with only the package's declared variables. [L16]
Example: runs one package once with exec, with no install step and no leftover state. [L18]
The binary stays cached in the object store, so repeat runs of the same version skip the download. [L22]
exec leaves no candidate symlink and no current pointer behind. [L22]
exec suits one-off tasks and CI runs that need reproducible isolation; daily tools are better installed. [L25]
Multiple packages passed before the double dash have their environments merged in declaration order. [L29]
Example: Bun and Node both end up on PATH inside one exec invocation. [L31]
exec re-resolves the package on every call, while install gives a persistent, named, offline-ready install. [L40]
install stores the binary content-addressed and creates a candidate symlink whose path never changes. [L42]
Two tags that resolve to the same binary build occupy only one object on disk. [L42]
which --candidate returns the stable candidate path without re-resolving, which suits build scripts and IDE configs. [L48]
Unlike apt install, ocx install needs no root and keeps multiple versions side by side. [L54]
In CI, package pull downloads into the object store without creating candidate or current symlinks. [L58]
The setup-ocx GitHub Action installs ocx, pulls the project toolchain, and replays the environment in one step. [L61]
A candidate path includes the tag, so upgrading leaves configs pinned to the old candidate until they are edited. [L68]
select adds a floating current pointer to the chosen version, so references to current pick up upgrades automatically. [L70]
install with the select flag combines installation and selection in one step. [L72]
select switches between installed versions, and deselect removes the active pointer without uninstalling. [L78]
The pattern matches SDKMAN and nvm default aliases, but applies to any binary package with no plugin. [L82]
Because current never changes its own path, shell profiles and IDE settings need no edits after an upgrade. [L86]
uninstall removes the candidate symlink and its back-reference, and keeps the binary unless purge is given and refs are empty. [L94]
uninstall removes the symlink immediately, while clean removes every unreferenced object in one pass. [L102]
Packages declare their environment variables in metadata.json, so manual syncing of paths is unnecessary. [L110]
package env resolves declarations relative to the installed path, and package exec injects them into a clean child process. [L112]
The installer writes env.sh, which calls ocx self activate at shell startup, so activation works before ocx is on PATH. [L118]
The PATH entry points at the current symlink, so the profile stays valid across upgrades. [L118]
Example: ocx --global add uv:0.10 installs a package and puts its binaries on PATH in every new shell. [L121]
Path-type variables such as PATH are prepended to existing values, while constant variables replace them. [L125]
Declaring project tools once and locking them to digests gives every contributor and CI runner the same binaries. [L138]
init writes a minimal ocx.toml, add resolves tags to per-platform digests and writes ocx.lock, and exec runs with the locked environment. [L144]
On bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell and elvish the toolchain lands on PATH automatically when you cd into the project. [L146]
nushell, the strict POSIX shells and Windows Batch need direnv, which ocx direnv init sets up. [L148]
The VSCode extension brings the project toolchain into editor terminals and tasks. [L152]
With no setup, a config.toml in OCX_HOME sets persistent defaults such as a private registry hostname. [L168]
Environment variables and CLI flags always override values from config files. [L174]
index catalog and index list let you browse what the registry offers before installing. [L177]
